clinical.citation: Array-Based Comparative Genomic Hybridization Analysis in Children with Developmental Delay/Intellectual Disability (PMID: 36249514)

variants.description: De novo multi-gene CNV (copy-number type not stated in the available text) that includes ATRN together with PTPRA, GNRH2, MRPS26, OXT, AVP, LZTS3, ITPA, SLC4A11, ADAM33, SIGLEC1 and HSPA12B (case 30, F-4). ATRN is not specifically implicated.
phenotypes: Developmental delay/intellectual disability (cohort inclusion criterion; individual features not given in the available text)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Classified as a de novo variant of uncertain significance (VUS) with no subclassification. The CNV spans many genes and ATRN is not singled out as causal.
clinical.center_country: Not stated in the available text (likely Turkey)

model_organism.citation: Post-developmental extracellular proteoglycan maintenance in attractin-deficient mice (PMID: 32580758)
phenotypes: Severe loss of extracellular proteoglycan between kidney tubules
Loss of glycosylated material in the intratubular brush border
Depleted extracellular matrix between hepatocytes in the liver
Swollen liver sinuses
Aberrant proteoglycan-dependent space of Disse
Generalized defect in extracellular proteoglycan deposition (consistent with a secretory vesicle pathway defect)

model_organism.citation: Attractin Participates in Schizophrenia by Affecting Testosterone Levels (PMID: 34869343)
phenotypes: More pronounced attack behavior in adult atrn-/- fish in tracking analysis
Elevated testosterone levels
Upregulation of cyp51 and hsd17b7 (testosterone synthesis genes) in brains of adults and larvae

model_organism.citation: Agouti protein, mahogunin, and attractin in pheomelanogenesis and melanoblast-like alteration of melanocytes: a cAMP-independent pathway (PMID: 19493315)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (spontaneous mutant Atrn mg-3J/mg-3J melanocyte line, in vitro)
phenotypes: Atrn-null melanocytes still responded to ASIP and ASIP-YY with reduced cAMP
Only ASIP, not ASIP-YY, altered proliferation and (in part) shape of Atrn-null melanocytes
Supports a cAMP-independent ASIP-MC1R pathway requiring attractin and mahogunin

model_organism.citation: Alkbh4 and Atrn Act Maternally to Regulate Zebrafish Epiboly (PMID: 28924386)
phenotypes: Maternal Atrn plays a role similar to Alkbh4 in embryonic morphogenesis
Regulates actomyosin formation
Regulates epiboly during gastrulation (epiboly defects)
Atrn interacts with active Alkbh4 to regulate actin demethylation

model_organism.citation: Mitochondrial dysfunction precedes neurodegeneration in mahogunin (Mgrn1) mutant mice (PMID: 17720281)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (spontaneous Atrn mutant mice, studied alongside Mgrn1 mutants)
phenotypes: Mitochondrial dysfunction in Atrn mutant brains
Increased oxidative stress in Atrn mutant brains
Age-dependent spongiform neurodegeneration in Atrn- and Mgrn1-deficient mice

model_organism.citation: RML prions act through Mahogunin and Attractin-independent pathways (PMID: 23787699)
phenotypes: Atrn null mice accumulate brain vacuoles resembling prion disease, but without protease-resistant PrP-scrapie accumulation and without becoming sick
Loss of ATRN had no effect on onset or progression of RML prion disease after intracerebral inoculation

model_organism.citation: Absence-like and tonic seizures in aspartoacylase/attractin double-mutant mice (PMID: 17460362)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (Aspa knockout combined with Atrn mg-3J mutant allele, double homozygous)
phenotypes: Absence-like and tonic seizures
5-7 Hz spike-wave-like complexes and low voltage fast waves on EEG
Simultaneous loss of Aspa and Atrn causes epileptic seizures

model_organism.citation: Biochemical and genetic studies of pigment-type switching (PMID: 11041357)
phenotypes: mahogany (Atrn) mutation suppresses the pigmentary effects of Agouti
mahogany suppresses the effects of Ay on pigmentation and body weight
mg is genetically upstream of Mc1r

model_organism.citation: Positional cloning of rat mutant genes reveals new functions of these genes (PMID: 36058846)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (spontaneous zitter mutation, 8-bp splice donor deletion in Atrn)
phenotypes: Marked reduction of membrane-bound Atrn expression in zitter rat brain
Neurological impairments and neurodegenerative changes
Darkened coat color when introduced into agouti rats
Myelination-related abnormalities

biological.citation: Mutation of the attractin gene impairs working memory in rats (PMID: 36621889)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9 ATRN-G505C knock-in rats showed longer latency and distance to the escape platform in the Morris water maze working-memory test. Myelin basic protein (MBP) expression was reduced on western blot, suggesting that ATRN mutation impairs spatial cognition through reduced MBP.

biological.citation: Attractin Gene Deficiency in Rats Leads to Impairments in Both Activity and Spatial Learning and Memory (PMID: 34000322)
biological.summary: ATRN-G505C knock-in rats (exon 9) showed impaired Morris water maze performance and reduced open field distance. BDNF expression was significantly reduced by western blot and immunohistochemistry, linking ATRN to learning, memory and neurodegeneration-related changes.

biological.citation: Post-developmental extracellular proteoglycan maintenance in attractin-deficient mice (PMID: 32580758)
biological.summary: Atrn-mutant mice lose extracellular proteoglycan in kidney and liver and show disrupted space of Disse. This supports a role for transmembrane attractin in the secretory vesicle/proteoglycan deposition pathway.

biological.citation: The neuroprotective role of attractin in neurodegeneration (PMID: 16860906)
biological.summary: Atrn knockdown worsened and Atrn overexpression protected against neuronal death induced by MPP+ and lactacystin. Atrn also modulated cytochrome c and AIF release, implicating it in mitochondrial function. Most mouse dopaminergic neurons express Atrn, and expression declines with age.

Atrn-null mice show dark fur, spongiform neurodegeneration, hypomyelination, tremor and reduced adiposity. Atrnl1 mutants are normal, but a beta-actin-driven Atrnl1 transgene rescues the agouti banding and delays neurodegeneration in Atrn-null mice. The two paralogs are therefore redundant in gain-of-function but not loss-of-function settings.

biological.citation: The myelin vacuolation (mv) rat with a null mutation in the attractin gene (PMID: 12379762)
biological.summary: The mv rat has a genomic deletion including Atrn exon 1 and no Atrn mRNA in brain. It shows tremor and CNS myelin vacuolation with splitting of myelin lamellae. The phenotype maps to the Atrn locus and is allelic with zitter.

biological.citation: Does human attractin have DP4 activity? (PMID: 17261078)
biological.summary: Attractin purified from human plasma has no intrinsic DP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase 4) activity; the activity came from a DP4 impurity. Recombinant attractin isoforms also lacked DP4 activity, so attractin likely acts as a receptor or adhesion protein rather than a protease.

biological.citation: Molecular and phenotypic analysis of Attractin mutant mice (PMID: 11514456)
biological.summary: Three Atrn alleles (mg-3J, mg, mg-L) cause loss-of-function pigmentation and neurodegeneration phenotypes, with severity tracking normal Atrn mRNA levels. Mutants have reduced body weight and adiposity and increased locomotor activity despite normal food intake, suggesting increased energy expenditure. Pigmentation is more sensitive to Atrn mRNA levels than the other phenotypes.

biological.citation: Attractin Participates in Schizophrenia by Affecting Testosterone Levels (PMID: 34869343)
biological.summary: atrn-/- zebrafish show increased attack behavior, elevated testosterone, and upregulated cyp51 and hsd17b7 in the brain. In patients, ATRN expression was reduced in a subset of extreme-phenotype subjects. Fourteen subjects carrying ATRN mutations all had abnormal testosterone, linking ATRN to sex-dimorphic psychiatric phenotypes.
biological.sample_size: 9,008 psychiatric patients, 247 controls; 14 ATRN mutation carriers

biological.citation: Agouti protein, mahogunin, and attractin in pheomelanogenesis and melanoblast-like alteration of melanocytes: a cAMP-independent pathway (PMID: 19493315)
biological.summary: Atrn-null (mg-3J) melanocytes still showed the cAMP response to ASIP but lacked its effects on proliferation and shape. This places attractin, together with mahogunin, in a cAMP-independent branch of ASIP-MC1R signaling.
